chunks.label: Asking how much
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask how much or how long, and push a question with surprise.
chunks.interference: Dore gurai is neutral; dore dake and donna ni are usually emotional.

chunks.label: Very and really
chunks.rationale: Lets you say 'really', 'super' and 'dead tired' at the right strength.
chunks.interference: Zuibun is about a surprising amount or change, not a plain 'very'.

chunks.label: So-so and fairly
chunks.rationale: Lets you give a modest, middle-of-the-road answer.
chunks.interference: Maamaa works alone as a reply; sorenari ni and aru teido modify a verb.

chunks.label: Feelings as sounds
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you're nervous, excited, annoyed, let down or relieved.
chunks.interference: Dokidoki includes nerves; wakuwaku is pure happy excitement.

chunks.label: Just now, in no time
chunks.rationale: Lets you say when something happened or must be done.
chunks.interference: Itsu no ma ni is about not noticing; atto iu ma ni is about speed.

chunks.label: As usual, basically
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe your normal routine and habits.

chunks.label: Early, last-minute, hectic
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about timing and pace: early, cutting it close, rushed or relaxed.
chunks.interference: Girigiri is about the limit; batabata is about being busy.

chunks.label: Just a little
chunks.rationale: Lets you play down an amount or a thing.
chunks.interference: Tatta goes before numbers; hon no and chotto shita go before nouns.

chunks.label: More and more
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe change: fast, gradual or still growing.
chunks.interference: Dondon is about speed; masumasu is about degree.

chunks.label: Enough and complete
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something is enough, plenty, nearly done or totally done.
chunks.interference: Juubun (enough) and juppun (ten minutes) share the same kanji.

chunks.label: Not at all, never
chunks.rationale: Lets you say 'not at all' and 'never' with force.
chunks.interference: All need a negative verb; kesshite is the solemn 'never'.

chunks.label: Quite a lot
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something has changed a lot or is seriously so.

chunks.label: Quietly and by accident
chunks.rationale: Lets you say how something was done: carelessly, vaguely, gently, secretly or without moving.
chunks.interference: Sotto means gently; kossori means without being seen.

chunks.label: Just right
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something fits, works or feels just right.
chunks.interference: Sukkiri is about feeling clear, not about fit.

chunks.label: At least, no more
chunks.rationale: Lets you set a minimum, a limit, or say what matters most.
chunks.interference: Semete is a wish; sukunakutomo is a factual minimum.

chunks.label: Giving it everything
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you'll go all out, together, and manage somehow.
chunks.interference: Seiippai is careful best effort; omoikkiri is holding nothing back.

chunks.label: For real and for sure
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you mean it, really want it, or were wrongly sure.
chunks.interference: Tekkiri is always a belief that turned out wrong.
